items.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001
items.q: But Bob Carsey was responsible for getting this music to me.

ctx.x: I can hear a lot further than what I can play. But Negro was so perfect. He can do anything I write, anything I do, he’s just right there. Just right on it. So it was a lot of fun. And those should come out this year so I’m looking forward to that. It would be fun to tour doing some of that music. And Paquito knew everything. These tunes that I thought

were really, I mean I went to Hawaii and they had this one tune. Nobody would know that, no piano anywhere near that with a singer. And he says, “Oh that’s — I know that, yeah.” And he started playing. He knew every tune I had on the album. Nobody knows all of it. But Bob Carsey was responsible for getting this music to me. You know, “Joanne, I think, listen to this one,” you know, he gave me a whole album to listen to. Some Piazzola, all different things.
Now there’s a name that seems to be on the hot list these days.
